**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 00:37
- [USER] User asked how to prepare potatoes for frying.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To prepare potatoes for frying, choose high-starch potatoes like Russet or Idaho potatoes for a crispy exterior and fluffy interior.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wash the potatoes thoroughly to remove dirt or debris.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Peel the potatoes using a vegetable peeler or a sharp knife.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cut the potatoes into desired shapes: thin slices for potato chips, sticks for French fries, or wedges for potato wedges.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for at least 30 minutes to remove excess starch for crispiness.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After soaking, drain the potatoes and pat them dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Heat a pot of oil (vegetable or peanut oil) to 350°F (175°C) to 375°F (190°C) for frying.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Carefully add the potatoes to the hot oil in batches, avoiding overcrowding the pot.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Fry the potatoes until golden brown and crispy, then remove them with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Season the fried potatoes with salt and any other desired seasonings, and serve hot.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Use caution when working with hot oil and never leave it unattended.
